audio_caption: The clip begins with a male speaker referencing a previous video he created about the Glazers' strategy at Manchester United. He advises viewers to watch the linked video, explaining that his argument is that the Glazers' strategy is now based around a top four finish rather than winning trophies. His tone suggests he's delivering an important message.

The clip starts with a passionate male speaker, claiming to "go a step further and prove to you how the Glazers are thieves" at Manchester United. He highlights how their leveraged buyout deal back in 2005 using excellent research conducted by Swiss Ramble made them leaches. He emphasizes the importance of liking and sharing the video because "Glazers out." Then he asks if these videos will make any difference, and answers that he won't ignore it. He wants to talk about it and show with "numbers and evidence the true scale of the thievery." Then there's a short, nondescript noise.

The clip begins with a male speaker asserting that past success at United has been "in spite of the Glazers," claiming that someone "overachieved in comparison." He then announces the topic for the video will focus on evidence provided with numbers by Swiss Ramble. The speaker encourages the audience to follow a link to their blog that focuses on the business side of football. He thanks Swiss Ramble, and tells his audience that the video may not be enjoyable but is necessary for them to watch and share so that they understand "the scale of the the-bu that's happened at United since 2005."

The clip begins with a single male speaker saying "Five". He then discusses the Swiss Ramble analysis of the last five years of the Premier League, covering 20 clubs. The speaker suggests to "take a look at all 20 at once" and the financing. The speaker maintains a conversational tone throughout.

A male speaker lists financial figures related to football clubs, noting investments made by Chelsea, Manchester City, and Liverpool, then pointing out that Manchester United's owners are extracting money instead of investing. The speaker delivers these figures with a slightly indignant tone.

The audio clip begins with an impassioned male voice accusing individuals of using a club as a "cash cow," dismissing spending on signings as related to the money taken out by said individuals. He clarifies that investment has been made in the pockets of these people. No music or ambient sounds are detected in the clip.

The clip starts with a single male speaker discussing a list, referencing the "United" team and noting their position at the bottom. He uses a frustrated tone, contrasting "Chelsea's investment" with United's payments to the Glazers. He emphasizes, "We are the only club to pay dividends to their owners", expressing outrage at what he perceives as theft. He ends with the assertion, "We all know what they are using United for." A slight pause, before he states, "and it’s not to get us back to winning the Premier League again."

A male speaker discusses financial matters, stating, "It's not just with the dividends that money is leaving United at a rapid rate," followed by, "Have a look at this in terms of the external financing." The tone is informative and somewhat serious. There is no audible music or background noise to suggest a specific setting.

The audio begins with a male speaker discussing financial losses of a football club. The speaker is clearly frustrated as they report an 80 million pound loss, which is the consequence of the current owners buying the club through a loan. He continues to express his distaste for the financial situation caused by the owners' loan, saying that "it's fucked" and that "they used their assets as leverage".

The clip features one male speaker who is upset. He talks about the banks making "hundreds and hundreds of millions from United," and "over 111 million in the last 5-6 years alone in dividends." He further says "hundreds of millions when they eventually sell United".

The audio clip begins with a male speaker passionately condemning the current state of Manchester United, saying the only losers are "Manchester United as a football club, and the fans." The speaker expresses frustration, saying the club is no longer a football club but "a business first," a cash cow, a side project for the owners. The speaker then contrasts this with the investment made in other clubs like Manchester City and Liverpool. They lament that in the last five years, the club has paid £209 million "for the Glazer's ownership structure," and in the last 10 years, spent £838 million on financing. The speaker then concludes his message with a strong condemnation of the Glazers, saying "Fuck the Glazers, fuck their ownership of United."

The audio begins with a male speaker discussing "366, the success" of a team between 2006 and 2009, asserting this was "not because of the Glazers" but "in spite of" them. He continues to explain how "Fergie" managed to rebuild a "title-winning team". The speaker's tone is assertive and analytical.

The clip begins with a male speaker expressing concerns about underinvestment compared to rivals, mentioning specific player signings like "Donny van de Beek" and "Sergio Regulon," and criticizing the club's financial decisions. He mentions that the manager has not been backed by the club and Ferguson's call when he left as manager. He further points out substantial interest repayments and an overall large sum that has left the club. The speaker expresses dismay and disapproval.

The audio begins with an individual, seemingly male, expressing frustration, stating "it just pisses me off". He argues that criticizing player signings like Harry Maguire misses the "scale and the structure of the thievery" at United under the Glazers, considering spending on players insignificant compared to constant dividends and interest repayments. He emphasizes that the whole leveraged buyout was a "complete and utter farce," concluding with a sense of helplessness, but insists "it is important that we do not ignore it."

The clip starts with an impassioned male speaker encouraging fans to do whatever they can to voice their concerns, including using hashtags and highlighting the negative impact of the current owners. The speaker’s tone is serious and persuasive, as he elaborates on the financial impact on the club and asserts other clubs are investing more effectively. He suggests the team is a business first, no longer a football club. The speaker then uses stronger language and asserts, "We're not a football club anymore."

The clip begins with a male speaker discussing "the cost of lies", citing an amount paid in interest repayments and dividends. His tone is passionate and frustrated, directed at "the Glazers", expressing a desire for the message to be shared. There is a call to action, urging listeners to not ignore the "rotten" core of Manchester United. The audio concludes with a low frequency rumble.
